summary: VOIP Extension creation for ASBC requires 2nd save.
description: Product Requirement Violation: [P1544-PRQ-139](https://hillrom.jamacloud.com/perspective.req?docId=4823323&projectId=548)

For ASBCs, a VOIP extension endpoint is not being created on the initial save. The user has to save again to in order for a VOIP extension to be created. There is no documentation or warning to reflect this. Audio Station,  Staff Consoles, and RADs do not have this behavior. Once those devices are created, serialized, and save, a VOIP extension is created.
comment_summary: The defect reported that VOIP extension creation for the ASBC required a second save in ECT. Follow-up testing confirmed that the new ASBC extension registers as expected and audio could be opened after a single save, so the reported behavior did not persist. Existing test cases were used rather than a new build, with only a script update needed. The regression test passed in ST1 while the direct test executed in PDR_13/ST3 failed against a separate defect, under which that verification continues, and this defect was closed as Done.

impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Updated the stored procedure that inserts the Device record and ASBCConfig record into their respective tables and in that order. The update made checks if the VOIPExtension parameter is empty or null and if so, will create the concatenated VOIPExtension that is expected. This is done after the Device record is inserted, but before the ASBCConfig record is inserted. This is due to when the DeviceID is available, which is only after the row is added.   
This concatenation is the Address (A or B) followed by the device type (asbc), a hyphen, and then the primary key of that device.  
Previously, the behavior was such that this VOIPExtension field would not be created until after the ASBC record already exists which required the second save action.  
This scenario is quite specific and the change is not impactful to the system. Recommended verification includes deleting an asbc and recreating it - one associated with an audio station not serialized to a real device, and one associated with a real configured audio device.

Impact Assessment:  
NCP - Configuration - Database - Trivial

Platform Impact:  
N/A

Regression Meeting:  
Date - 01/13/2025  
Attendees - Jaime Vaquera (Quality Engineering), Alec Kaufman (Development Engineering)  
Minutes - The change is only a trivial updated stored procedure with no change to the HRDB deployment. The direct test will handle the actual ASBC removal and addition functionality. The regression tests will be simple HRDB deployment of a new install and an upgrade scenerio just to sanity that deployment is not affected. 

Additional Software Components:  
N/A
steps_taken: Create a patient location in the nursing unit  
Add a bed designator  
Save  
Add Audio Station, serialized and configure.  
Optional - save configuration (same behavior happens with or without this option)  
Add the ASBC and configure it while referencing it to the room's audio station.    
Save  
Connect a Pillow Speaker to the ASBC  
Place a Normal from the Pillow Speaker
actual_results: Cannot answer the call from the Staff Console. Answer button is greyed out and lifting handset does not open audio. 

Without any notice, The ASBC properties shows a missing VOIP Extension even though the ASBC is connected to the Audio Station.
expected_results: Call is answered at the Staff Console and audio is open between the pillow speaker and Console.
work_around: Saving again in ECT will result in a VOIP extension being created and audio being functional after save.

Another workflow to avoid this is by creating the audio station and ASBC but do not serialize the audio station.   
Save the configuration in ECT  
Serialize the audio station and save again.  
Place a call from the Pillow Speaker connected to the ASBC  
Answer call and audio opens.

root_cause_summary: Bad U1_PWR and bad audio amplifier U9_AUD likely due to an ESD event or hot plugging or a known issue with the bed connector cable (bent pins).
investigation_details: **HW Investigation**

Device would not power up because all power rails were shorted to Ground, which trips fuse RT1. So it failed to initialize on the DFCT (no logs to attach). Confirmed with DMM continuity test that U1_PWR input and output were shorted (pins 2 and 4). Removed U1_PWR and +5V rail was still shorted to Ground but other power rails were normal resistance. U9_AUD was removed and +5V rail and ground were no longer shorted.

Replaced U1_PWR and U9_AUD with known good components. Device now passes DFCT tests, see attached logs. Note that VPD read/write test was skipped in case there were other issues that required firmware investigation.

We have seen this issue before, resulting from bent pins on the bed connector cable, hot plugging, ESD, etc. (Reference https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1866, https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1685, https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-1075  and others.)

Conclusion: Bad U1_PWR and bad audio amplifier U9_AUD likely due to an ESD event or hot plugging or a known issue with the bed connector cable (bent pins).

comment_summary: Multiple SRS units failed at a customer site and were returned for analysis; all four returned units had a shorted LM4675 audio amplifier, with the short between +5V and common, leaving the SRS apparently dead and unable to be rebooted. Database event review showed that around the time of the Lost Primary Audio Station alerts the affected rooms had various unrelated call types (Normal Call, Bed Disconnect, Pillow Speaker Disconnect, Staff Call), with some rooms looping in and out of the Lost Primary Audio Station alert until the SRS was replaced. The same pattern then appeared at a second customer, and syslogs were collected per device for several rooms, while acoustic settings were compared against a working system. The thread ends without an identified cause for the amplifier shorts.

text: Environment: NNC and Voalte Nurse Call - All Versions

Non-Medical Device Complaints (Excel Medical, Voalte Mobile, etc.)

Explanation

---

Assign this KB to the complaint case when the following criteria are met:

- A case has been escalated to Tier 2 either for investigation or KB article evaluation, and it is determined that no technical KB article is applicable.
- Cases that have been determined as a known defect or a change request, and have a valid defect or change request ID present.
- Investigations which find a ‘one-off’ or unique error, or an error not likely to recur.
- Cases where the **Investigation Summary → Main and Sub Assembly → Reason** codes contain any of the following:
    - **3rd Party : (...)**
    - **Cancelled on customer request**
    - **Configuration Change Required/Requested** *(where the product is working as designed but the customer is requesting configuration changes)*** ** 
    - **Duplicate case**
    - **No details provided**
    - **No problem found/Could not reproduce**
    - **No response from user**
    - **User Interface/Interaction Error** *(where the product is working as designed but the end user needed to be educated on the proper use)  
*
- Cases where the** Reason** code contains \<***software**\>* **misconfigured **or *\<**hardware**\>*** misinstalled**, and proper procedure for those codes can be found in Help Center.  
  
- Please utilize this KB for complaints following the Non-Medical Device workflow. (Excel Medical, Voalte Mobile, etc.)

summary: NC-ENT-GRS10 Making a 3 Tone Beeping Noise/Sporadic stuck calls
description: Acct# 802097

Acct name:Mount Nittany Medical Center

NC Version: 4.2.000

  
Initial report: GRS10s are beeping with no calls or alerts active. Calls are also being stuck on child devices. All of this began post last upgrade to 4.2.

Current status: After purging the configuration on the effected GRS10s the beeping with no active calls ceased. Has not returned yet but this is the second iteration of the customer having a GRS10 toning without having an active call/alert. The calls getting stuck on the child devices don’t follow normal procedure for placing and cancelling calls. See troubleshooting summary.  
  
Request: Confirm why GRS10s are having this beeping issue with no active calls/alerts.

Confirm why calls are getting stuck on child devices.
comment_summary: A site reported GRS10s emitting a three-tone beeping noise with no active calls or alerts, together with sporadic stuck calls where a call placed in one room remained active on a GRS5 in another room with no matching active call in the database. Raising APLMOD logging to level 7 on an affected RCB confirmed a tone being played repeatedly with no reference to a current call, and the stuck call cleared after rebooting the room; purging the configuration of a GRS10 resolved a beeping instance. The pattern identified was that affected calls were all configured "display at patient station: always", only old hardware was involved (GRS5 not GRS7, RCB not RCB3, AGAS not GRS10H), and it occurred in units where an AGAS acts as the NUC, suggesting a timing issue. Replacing the AGAS NUC with an RCB3 NUC in an affected unit stopped recurrences there and the approach was extended to other units, while merely turning logging up also appeared to change the timing and stop the problem; the thread concludes it is a timing issue with no single identifiable cause, expected to be corrected by the significant changes in 4.2.200.

root_cause_summary: This is a timing issue.  And, while we can’t point at anyting and say “this is the cause”, things have changed significantly in 4.2.200 which is expected to correct the issue. https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/NC-386#icft=NC-386 is the item the work was done under.  

[https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/NC-386](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/NC-386)
investigation_details: have been looking thru logs and looking at devices where this has happened.   
  
characteristics:

1. call is placed, annunciates normally and is eventually canceled.  Call remains active on a GRS5
2. the common characteristics for call configuration so far is that they have all been “display at patient station: always”
3. only has been observed on old hardware: grs5, not grs7, rcb, not rcb3, agas not grs10h
4. happens in units that have an AGAS as a nuc
5. seems to be some sort of timing issue, this could also be a coincidence, turning up logging on devices for a unit where this happens as frequently as anywhere, which is still very infrequently, and it has not happened in that unit since.

Hospital has been adding an rcb3 nuc to units where this has happened and we have not seen a re-occurrence in those units since.
troubleshooting_steps: Received call from Sam Gormont around 8:45 am. Called Sam back. He confirmed the issue has returned with GRS10 beeping with no calls/alerts.  
Requested he confirm what console he is at. He gave the ip address 172.16.26.1 which belongs to the GRS10 NUC for 3 North.  
Further probing revealed the beeping was related to a accurate bed offline alert. Walked Sam through steps for checking call.  
Cleared alert after adjusting power cable for bed. Confirmed now we have no beeping.  
Confirmed beeping with no active calls or alerts has not reoccured since purging config consoles.  
Sam then brought up another stuck call on a GRS5. GRS5 for room W 362 is showing a call from room N 376.  
This call has been on the waitlist for 52 hours. Vnc into both GRS5s. Confirmed N 376 does not show a active call.  
Restarted messaging service on the off chance nursefollower issue could have applied. No change. Restarted Device service. No change.  
While the device service was down the GRS5 for W 362 never rebooted any alerts. It also still held on to the stuck normal call.  
Resetting audio did nothing. Placed another normal call from N 376 to W 362. Our existing normal call is the only call that shows.  
Although audio does still open between the two as of we accepted a call that we never receive. Sam did confirm he can hear the feedback on the audio station confirming audio is open.  
When checking the syslogs for evidence of audio being opened between the two devices. Did not find a voip transaction for the call.  
Sam confirmed rebooting the effected room will fix it but it will return. Requested we reboot to clear and try to replicate.  
Rebooted room W 362. Confirmed now call is cleared. Placed another normal call from N 376. No call ever appeared although audio does open still without being accepted.  
Sam confirmed this has only been a issue since upgrading. He stated prior to the upgrade they rarely had a open Nursecall case. Now they have frequent cases surrounding stuck calls.  
Confirmed i would continue to investigate but this will likely need a RCA. Sam confirmed. Checked software version for all devices. Confirmed they are all on the correct version.  
Site does have multiple lost secondary alerts. Thought this was related to a down CCD/PBX. Did not find a CCD/PBX for the site. Further probing revealed the site has multiple unserialized devices connected.
troubleshooting_results: Call is cleared but customer would like confirmation on why they are getting stuck.
verification_summary: Identified Tech Story https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/browse/NC-386#icft=NC-386 to address WebSocket issues. Fix planned for 4.2.200 software release.
rca_review_comments: This is a timing issue.  And, while we can’t point at anyting and say “this is the cause”, things have changed significantly in 4.2.200 which is expected to correct the issue. NC-386 is the item the work was done under.

summary: Staff Stations Toning despite no calls being active
description: Issue was discovered at St Joseph Candler after an upgrade to 3.9.102.

Staff Stations were found to be toning for a call despite no call being active on the GRS-5 or the GRS-10.  Rebooting all rooms from the GRS-10 and rebooting the GRS-10 itself resolves the issue.

Issue has only occurred once per unit since the upgrade.  After the devices were rebooted we have not received additional reports of the issue.

Customer is not using Nurse Follower.
comment_summary: Staff stations at a site were toning although no calls were active. The condition was first thought to be a one-off, but it recurred on the same floor about two weeks later and was cleared by rebooting all the rooms and the GRS-10. Advanced service logs and syslogs were collected for both occurrences, and the affected stations were confirmed to be mostly GRS-5s rather than SRS devices. The site was asked to call while the fault is happening so further troubleshooting could be done, and no further occurrences were reported, so no cause or change is established in the thread.

comment_summary: A site reported static and echo in GRS10 audio with GRS5s in patient rooms and a mix of third-party and Hillrom/Curbell pillow speakers in use. Engineering requested the specific device chain and pillow speaker models, and sample pillow speakers were shipped for lab testing so acoustic settings could be investigated and adjusted. Review of the customer's reported symptoms explained several of them as expected behavior: a surround effect because audio comes from both the pillow speaker and bed speakers depending on distance, clear pillow speaker audio when the bed is unplugged, and the system falling back to bed speakers plus the GRS5 microphone when the pillow speaker is unplugged, while the static and echo were expected to depend on pillow speaker brand and model. The site's acoustic settings were modified according to an attached settings document, and the customer later confirmed the audio issues had subsided after those changes and after replacing a few suspect pillow speakers.

text: Environment: NNC and Voalte Nurse Call - All Versions

Non-Medical Device Complaints (Excel Medical, Voalte Mobile, etc.)

Explanation

---

Assign this KB to the complaint case when the following criteria are met:

- A case has been escalated to Tier 2 either for investigation or KB article evaluation, and it is determined that no technical KB article is applicable.
- Cases that have been determined as a known defect or a change request, and have a valid defect or change request ID present.
- Investigations which find a ‘one-off’ or unique error, or an error not likely to recur.
- Cases where the **Investigation Summary → Main and Sub Assembly → Reason** codes contain any of the following:
    - **3rd Party : (...)**
    - **Cancelled on customer request**
    - **Configuration Change Required/Requested** *(where the product is working as designed but the customer is requesting configuration changes)*** ** 
    - **Duplicate case**
    - **No details provided**
    - **No problem found/Could not reproduce**
    - **No response from user**
    - **User Interface/Interaction Error** *(where the product is working as designed but the end user needed to be educated on the proper use)  
*
- Cases where the** Reason** code contains \<***software**\>* **misconfigured **or *\<**hardware**\>*** misinstalled**, and proper procedure for those codes can be found in Help Center.  
  
- Please utilize this KB for complaints following the Non-Medical Device workflow. (Excel Medical, Voalte Mobile, etc.)

rationale: Nothing was observable at the time of the remote check - no calls and no system alerts on the GRS10 - and the report was never reproduced, so no failure mode is available to corroborate; the beeping candidates do not fit (RCA-107 was reclassified as install-time configuration noise, RCA-1828 is a 4.2.000 post-upgrade GRS10 beeping issue while this site runs 4.0.404, and RCA-523 required toning that persisted until the rooms and console were rebooted).
